_README: Shape of the price map read by excel_extractor/extractor/pricing.py. Copy this file to
configs/model_pricing.json and fill in the rates, or point MODEL_PRICING_FILE somewhere else.
Every rate here is null on purpose: no numbers ship with the repo, because a rate is a contract
question rather than a code question.
There are two places rates can live, and both are optional. `models` is keyed by the exact model
id a run records; `tiers` is keyed by the pipeline's tier name. A model entry wins when one
exists for the id that ran, and the tier entry is the fallback. Each priced tier reports which
of the two answered, as `rates_basis` ('model' or 'tier') and `rates_key`.
Use `models` when one file has to price two providers. A tier name says how important a call was,
not what it cost: `high` is claude-opus-5 on --provider ica and a gpt-5 model on --provider azure,
at completely different rates. A tier-only file cannot tell those apart. A file with only `tiers`
still works exactly as before, which is what every price map written for the Claude-only path is.
Rates are USD per million tokens. The keys are the same in both sections:
model            the gateway model id the rates were written for. Optional inside `models`,
where the key already is the model id. Inside `tiers` it is what lets a run
notice the tier now runs something else: the tier is still priced (the rate is
per tier) but is named in `model_mismatch` so the swap is visible.
in               new, uncached input tokens.
cache_read       input tokens served from the prompt cache — about 0.1x `in`. Both providers
report this class, so fill it in for GPT models too.
cache_write_5m   input tokens written into a 5-minute cache entry — about 1.25x `in`.
cache_write_1h   input tokens written into a 1-hour cache entry — about 2x `in`.
out              output tokens, extended thinking / reasoning included.
cache_write_billed   set this to false for a model whose provider does not bill cache writes as
their own class. OpenAI is the case that needs it: its prompt caching is
automatic and a write is not a billed line, so there is no rate to write down.
Both write columns then become an explicit 0 and the entry prices normally.
Leave it out (or true) for Claude models, which do bill writes. The arithmetic
is the same either way — a GPT reply reports 0 cache-write tokens — but this
keeps 'declared free' from looking like 'rate unknown'.
The two write columns exist because a cache write is the one class whose rate depends on how
long the entry is asked to live. MODEL_CACHE_TTL picks the lifetime for the run (1h by default)
and pricing.py prices the matching column, naming it as `cache_ttl` in the cost block. A file
that carries a single `cache_write` key instead still works — that rate is then used for either
lifetime, which is only correct if you know which one the run used.
How it degrades, so a missing rate can never quietly become a wrong total:
* A tier is priced only when ALL FOUR of its rates are numbers. A tier with any null or
missing rate contributes nothing and is named in `unpriced_tiers`.
* With no usable rates for any tier, the cost block reports `priced: false` and carries no
dollar figures at all.
* A tier that ran more than one model over the run — the Azure→ICA fallback latching part-way
through — is named in `mixed_model_tiers`. Its tokens were billed against two price lists and
only one can be applied, so its total is wrong by the rate difference on the earlier model's
share, and it says so rather than looking clean.
* An unreadable or malformed file complains on stderr and is treated as absent. Pricing is a
reporting nicety appended after the work is done, so it never fails a run.
Tier names are the pipeline's own, from otl/llm_adapter._NODE_TIER. Note the third one is
`light`, not `low`. Model keys must match whatever the run resolves — ICA_MODEL_<TIER> or
AZURE_MODEL_<TIER> in .env, else the defaults in extractor/llm.py._TIER_DEFAULTS.
